topic: Solution Concentration, Solubility, Acids, Bases, and Salts
key_concepts: Mass/volume percent equals mass of solute in grams divided by volume of solution in millil
Solubility is the ability of a solute to dissolve in a solvent
Concentration, temperature, stirring or mixing, and particle size affect solubility
Unsaturated, saturated, and supersaturated solutions compare the amount of solute to its s
At 25°C, salt has a solubility of 35.7 g per 100 mL of water
Higher temperature increases particle kinetic energy and helps solute dissolve faster
Stirring spreads solute particles and helps them dissolve faster
Smaller solute particles have more exposed surface area and dissolve faster
Acids release hydrogen ions, bases release hydroxide ions, and salts form from acid-base r
The pH scale measures acidity or basicity from 0 to 14, with pH 7 neutral
